scope: Single substantial subscription-agent creation plus bounded native model continuation; not campaign qualification
intent: Make a substantial Sonic Advance × Metroid Zero Mission exploration mashup: retain Sonic momentum and original campaign, but reshape the first-act route around collecting two distinct Metroid capabilities, opening a matching native ability barrier, and managing nearby alien/recharge encounters. Put the early two relics and one matching gate on a practical visible route so the native testing bot can demonstrate acquisition and barrier opening. Change connected progression and resource/ecology decisions, not the title or a single constant. Keep the source-backed MZM mechanics recognizable and clearly say which bridges/enemies are authored. Do not claim a full Metroid remake or late-campaign completion.

attempts.reason: No authored placement or dependency error is supported by the supplied run. Missile and Morph were collected by observation frame 73 (upgrades=3, picked[0]=6). Sonic reached the visible missile seal at x600 and stopped near x586, consistent with the authored 14px collision boundary. All 23 action receipts contain only RIGHT; no B or R+B input was attempted, shots_fired remained 0, and 10 missiles remained available. The source requires a missile hit to open this seal. model_call_limit ended the run with 2 relics and 0 gates; it does not establish a broken gate or justify relocating the linked route. Preserve the world configuration, acceptance minimum, limits, confidence policy and partial native checkpoint; gate opening remains unproven.

repair.current_policy: Only actual decoded source-behavior contradictions trigger repair. Budget exhaustion never causes source rewrite.

timing.accounting: Build, boot, model and agent stages are nested in API elapsed. Continuation did not rebuild or boot. No CI timing or speedup claim. Direct policy regression is separately measured and not included in original API elapsed.
timing.baseline_note: Unchanged captured baseline rebuilt to identical bytes; variant timing uses same installed tools and original ROMs with changed world inputs.
